questions.question: Which kind of Node.js version should you install for real projects?
questions.explanation: LTS releases are the stable line meant for real projects, which is why the lesson tells you to always pick one.

questions.question: You run node tip.js 2400 4. At which index of process.argv is the value 2400?
questions.explanation: process.argv[0] is the Node binary and process.argv[1] is the script path, so your own arguments start at index 2.

questions.question: What does typing node on its own (with no file name) do?
options: Opens the REPL, where each line runs immediately
Prints the installed version and exits
Runs index.js in the current folder
questions.explanation: With no file, node opens the Read-Eval-Print Loop, a scratchpad for testing expressions; .exit leaves it.

questions.question: What does node --watch hello.js do?
options: Runs the script once with extra logging
Checks the script for syntax errors without running it
Reruns the script automatically every time you save the file
Opens the script in the editor
questions.explanation: The --watch flag restarts the program whenever the file changes; press Ctrl+C to stop it.
